args.text: [lane-wren] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale answers: if a site moves to a new server address, users keep being sent to the old one, causing outages or failed connections. (2) Slow recovery: after a fault or failover, traffic keeps going to a dead address until the cache expires. (3) Prolonged exposure to bad data: if a forged or poisoned answer is cached, it stays in place and misdirects users for longer.

[lane-wren] (1) Networks and servers fail in passing ways, so clients must retry, but a retry of a non-idempotent request can run the same action twice, such as charging a customer twice. (2) An idempotent request gives the same result however many times it is repeated, so retries stay safe and systems recover from faults without duplicate effects.

[lane-wren] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) It embeds a creation time, so anyone who sees an ID can tell roughly when the row was made, which may leak information. (2) It is 16 bytes, larger than a common 8-byte integer key, so indexes take more space, although its time ordering keeps inserts far friendlier than random UUIDs.

[lane-wren] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before it alters the main data, so nothing is lost if the system crashes. After a crash, the database replays the log to restore a consistent state, and the log also supports replication and point-in-time recovery.

[lane-wren] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Results stay comparable between runs, because an automatic update could change speed or behaviour and be mistaken for a real difference in the system under test. (2) Others can reproduce the numbers later, since the exact client used is known and can be installed again.
